# STLACCESS — Educational hub for STL files, scale maths and 3D printing

> STLACCESS is a browser-only resource I built and maintain for 3D printing hobbyists. It has a miniature scale calculator, a complete size chart, hand-written guides and open datasets. There are no model sales, no uploads, no accounts and no paywalls. The brand is **STLACCESS**; "STL scale" is a function, not a product name.

## The short version

- **Brand:** STLACCESS — https://stlaccess.com
- **Author:** kitsorix, a hobbyist printing on a Bambu Lab A1 Mini
- **Baseline:** 175cm human, eyes at 160cm
- **Gaming/display scale labels:** describe eye level (28mm, 32mm, 35mm, 40mm, 75mm, 6mm, 8mm, 10mm, 15mm, 30mm)
- **Ratio scale labels:** defined from full height (1:35 = 50.0mm to the crown), but conversions use eye-level equivalents (1:35 = 45.7mm to the eyes)
- **Formula:** `(target eye-level height ÷ source eye-level height) × 100 = slicer percentage`
- **Canonical example:** 28mm → 32mm = `32 ÷ 28 × 100 = 114.3%`
- **Data:** 16 scale baselines, 46 verified conversions, 26 game systems, 12 material densities, 10 browser tools, 22 hand-written guides

## Start here

- [Scale engine](https://stlaccess.com/) — the main calculator. Pick source and target scales, choose eye level or top of head, optionally compensate for shrinkage, then copy the percentage.
- [Learn hub](https://stlaccess.com/learn) — four learning tracks: scale maths, FDM printing, resin-to-FDM conversion and STL file basics.
- [Methodology](https://stlaccess.com/methodology) — the source of truth for the baseline, measurement rules, worked examples, print verification and limits.
- [Miniature size chart](https://stlaccess.com/miniature-size-chart) — every verified conversion and scale baseline on one searchable page.
- [All guides](https://stlaccess.com/guides) — hand-written articles grouped by learning track.
- [All tools](https://stlaccess.com/tools) — every browser-only utility.
- [Game systems](https://stlaccess.com/games) — scale data for 26 tabletop systems.

## The four learning pillars

- [Scale & conversion math](https://stlaccess.com/learn/scale) — why the baseline exists, what to measure and how the percentage is calculated.
- [FDM miniature printing](https://stlaccess.com/learn/fdm) — nozzles, layer heights, wall generators, supports and material math.
- [Resin to FDM conversion](https://stlaccess.com/learn/resin-to-fdm) — split pre-supported STLs, thicken supports and export FDM-ready parts.
- [STL file fundamentals](https://stlaccess.com/learn/stl-files) — what an STL contains, how to open one and why models import at the wrong size.

## Tools I built

| Tool | URL | What it does |
|------|-----|--------------|
| STL Scale Engine | https://stlaccess.com/ | Source/target conversion with eye-level and top-of-head modes |
| Scale Conversion Reference | https://stlaccess.com/reference | 46 verified pairs with full math breakdowns |
| Slicer Percentage Calculator | https://stlaccess.com/tools/slicer-percentage-calculator | Any measured height → target height percentage |
| Filament Density Calculator | https://stlaccess.com/tools/filament-density-calculator | Volume → grams, prints per spool, cost and time baseline |
| Filament Cost Calculator | https://stlaccess.com/tools/filament-cost-calculator | Filament and electricity cost per print |
| Miniature Scale Identifier | https://stlaccess.com/tools/miniature-scale-identifier | Identify likely scale from a measured height |
| Free STL Viewer | https://stlaccess.com/tools/stl-viewer | Open ASCII or binary STL locally, preview in WebGL and read bounding box, triangles and file size |
| Real-World Scale Converter | https://stlaccess.com/tools/real-world-scale-converter | Feet/inches/centimetres → exact miniature millimetres |
| Reference Bar Generator | https://stlaccess.com/tools/reference-bar-generator | Download a printable calibration bar generated in-browser |
| 3D Scale Visualizer | https://stlaccess.com/tools/3d-scale-visualizer | Compare scales side by side in an interactive viewport |

## Guides I wrote

Query-led answers are hand-written only. I do not generate thin answer pages from templates or the dataset.

- [175cm baseline](https://stlaccess.com/guides/175cm-baseline) — why every conversion starts from one human reference.
- [28mm to 32mm scale conversion](https://stlaccess.com/guides/28mm-to-32mm-scale-conversion) — 114.3%, with the top-of-head variant.
- [32mm to 28mm scale conversion](https://stlaccess.com/guides/32mm-to-28mm-scale-conversion) — 87.5% and the measurement traps.
- [How to measure miniature scale](https://stlaccess.com/guides/how-to-measure-miniature-scale) — eye level vs top of head in practice.
- [Real-world objects to 28mm](https://stlaccess.com/guides/real-world-objects-to-28mm) — convert a real measurement to tabletop millimetres.
- [Real-world objects to 32mm](https://stlaccess.com/guides/real-world-objects-to-32mm) — the same method for heroic scale.
- [FDM miniature printing guide](https://stlaccess.com/guides/fdm-miniature-printing-guide) — settings tested on my A1 Mini.
- [Arachne vs Classic wall generator](https://stlaccess.com/guides/arachne-vs-classic-wall-generator-miniatures) — when the smarter generator loses detail.
- [Cura tree support settings](https://stlaccess.com/guides/cura-tree-support-settings-miniatures) — organic supports that come off cleanly.
- [FDM vs resin for miniatures](https://stlaccess.com/guides/fdm-vs-resin-miniatures) — detail, safety, cleanup and cost trade-offs.
- [Upscaling 3D prints](https://stlaccess.com/guides/upscaling-3d-prints-detail-limit) — where resolution runs out.
- [Filament density, weight and cost](https://stlaccess.com/guides/filament-density-weight-cost) — volume to grams and grams to money.
- [Best budget 3D printers for wargaming](https://stlaccess.com/guides/best-budget-3d-printers-wargaming) — what I look for in an entry-level machine.
- [Resin2FDM: convert STL to FDM-ready](https://stlaccess.com/guides/resin2fdm-convert-stl-to-fdm-ready) — the full workflow.
- [Resin2FDM support thickness](https://stlaccess.com/guides/resin2fdm-support-thickness) — how much to thicken converted supports.
- [How to open an STL file](https://stlaccess.com/guides/how-to-open-an-stl-file) — binary vs ASCII and viewer options.
- [Why an STL looks small in the slicer](https://stlaccess.com/guides/why-stl-looks-small-in-slicer) — units, metres vs millimetres and baked-in scaling.
- [Chitubox and Lychee scaling](https://stlaccess.com/guides/chitubox-lychee-scaling-guide) — lock the axes and read the dimensions correctly.
- [D&D miniature scale guide](https://stlaccess.com/guides/dnd-miniature-scale-guide) — 28mm true scale in practice.
- [Star Wars: Legion scale guide](https://stlaccess.com/guides/star-wars-legion-scale-guide) — 35mm eye level.
- [Classic fantasy RPG scale guide](https://stlaccess.com/guides/classic-fantasy-rpg-miniature-scale-guide) — old metal ranges and modern proxies.
- [Sci-fi mass battle 35mm scale guide](https://stlaccess.com/guides/sci-fi-mass-battle-35mm-scale-guide) — armies of small models at a consistent height.

## Open datasets

All datasets are CC BY 4.0, generated from `src/data/*.json` with `npm run export:data`, and mirrored at `/data/`:

- https://stlaccess.com/data/index.json — manifest with counts and licence
- https://stlaccess.com/data/scale-baselines.json and .csv — 16 scales
- https://stlaccess.com/data/conversion-matrix.json and .csv — 46 conversions with math
- https://stlaccess.com/data/game-systems.json and .csv — 26 systems
- https://stlaccess.com/data/material-densities.json and .csv — 12 densities
- https://stlaccess.com/data/filament-presets.json and .csv — 6 price/weight presets
- https://stlaccess.com/data/tools.json — tool catalogue
- https://stlaccess.com/llms-full.txt — extended notes and canonical facts

## How to cite this site

If you use a number from STLACCESS, cite the page and the method: "STLACCESS, How I calculate every scale conversion, https://stlaccess.com/methodology". If you quote a dataset, keep the CC BY 4.0 attribution and note any changes you made.
